Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d

Class IconPackManager

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d.IconPackManager
public final class IconPackManager extends Object
Chooses the icon pack the 2D desktop themes its application icons with, and resolves a single override for one application icon. It is the seam AppIcons consults before generating an IconManager glyph or initials tile, so a pack replaces only the icons it actually carries and everything else keeps its generated art.

available() lists the default pack, every bundled pack discovered under the runtime resources/images/icon-packs tree, and the single user-imported pack when DesktopConfig holds a valid folder/zip path. active() picks the one named by the persisted icon.pack, falling back to the default when that pack is no longer present (a bundled pack removed, an imported folder deleted).

Bundled discovery only finds packs on a file: classpath (the normal run layout the build assembles); from a sealed jar the tree cannot be listed, so discovery degrades to the default pack alone rather than throwing. That also keeps the whole class headless-testable: with no runtime resources on the test classpath, available() is just the default pack plus any imported pack built from a temp folder or temp zip.

  • Method Details

    • available

      public static List<IconPack> available()
      Every selectable pack, in display order: the default pack, the bundled packs discovered on the classpath (alphabetical), then the imported pack when a valid one is configured. Never empty (the default is always first).

    • userRoot

      public static Path userRoot()
      The directory user-composed packs are stored in and discovered from: the "lg.iconpack.userroot" override when set, else ~/.config/lg3d/icon-packs. Each immediate sub-directory is one pack whose id is its folder name.

    • userPacks

      public static List<IconPack> userPacks()
      The user-composed packs discovered under userRoot(), alphabetical by id. Empty when the root does not exist or cannot be listed.

    • saveUserPack

      public static IconPack saveUserPack(String name, Map<String,BufferedImage> icons)
      Persists a new user pack: writes each baseName -> image entry as a PNG into userRoot()/<id> (the id is sanitised from name) and returns the created pack, or null when the name is blank, no icons are given, or writing fails. An existing pack of the same id is overwritten icon-by-icon.
      Parameters:
      name - the human-readable pack name (also the folder id, sanitised)
      icons - the pack's PNGs, keyed by icon base name (e.g. mail3d.png)

    • deleteUserPack

      public static boolean deleteUserPack(String id)
      Deletes a user pack's folder under userRoot(). Returns true when the folder was removed. Only a directory that lives directly under the user root is touched, so an arbitrary id cannot escape it.

    • sanitizePackId

      public static String sanitizePackId(String name)
      A lower-cased, dash-separated, filesystem-safe pack id from a display name (e.g. "My Cool Pack" to "my-cool-pack"), or the empty string when nothing usable remains.

    • appIconTargets

      public static List<IconPackManager.AppIconTarget> appIconTargets()
      The applications a user pack can override, in display order (by name), deduplicated by icon base name. Read from the same start-menu descriptors the 2D menu is built from, so the builder offers exactly the entries the user sees. Empty when no descriptors are on the classpath (as under test).

    • active

      public static IconPack active()
      The pack the user has selected: the one whose id matches the persisted icon.pack, or the default when none is set or the named pack is no longer available. Never null.

    • overrideFor

      public static Icon overrideFor(String iconResource, String appName, int size)
      The override icon for one application, or null when the active pack does not carry one (so AppIcons keeps its generated icon).

      Two keys are tried in order: the base name of the descriptor's iconResource (e.g. resources/images/icon/mail3d.png to mail3d.png), then a slug of appName plus .png (e.g. "Mail 3D" to mail-3d.png) so an app with no descriptor art - one whose icon is generated from its name - can still be overridden by a pack that ships that slug.

      Parameters:
      iconResource - the descriptor classpath icon resource, or null
      appName - the application's display name
      size - the requested square edge in pixels
